riddles.text: In Greek, it is βιβλίο (vivlio). Where do these live?
riddles.hint: Think where books are collected and borrowed.
riddles.explanation: From Greek βιβλιον (biblion) = book. The word library comes from Latin liber (book).

riddles.text: In German, linguists met where Kaffee flows. Where?
riddles.clue: Linguisten trafen sich, wo Kaffee fließt
riddles.hint: Not a pub. Somewhere with coffee.
riddles.explanation: Kaffee = coffee. Berlin intellectuals historically met in cafes.

riddles.text: In Spanish: El secreto esta en la iglesia. Where?
riddles.clue: El secreto está en la iglesia
riddles.explanation: Iglesia = church. Many secrets are kept in places of worship.

riddles.text: In Russian: Документы в архиве. Where?
riddles.explanation: Документы = documents, архиве = archive. Cyrillic was derived from Greek script.

riddles.text: These words share a root: Greek πατηρ, German Vater, English father, Spanish padre, Russian отец. What is the PIE root?
riddles.hint: Starts with asterisk p, ends with r.
riddles.explanation: All descend from Proto-Indo-European *pəter. This is what Elena was proving.

riddles.text: In Greek, καρδια means heart in German. What organ is this?
riddles.hint: It is in your chest and it beats.
riddles.explanation: Both trace back to PIE *ker. Greek root gives cardiac and cardiology.

riddles.text: In German, Gift means something deadly. What does it mean?
riddles.hint: Not something you want for your birthday.
riddles.explanation: German Gift = poison, while English gift comes from Old Norse.

riddles.text: This Russian word мать shares its root with English mother. What does it mean?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *meh2ter. All words are cognates.

riddles.text: In Spanish, libro means book. What Latin word connects it to library?
riddles.hint: Latin word for book, also in liberate.
riddles.explanation: From Latin liber (book), which gives library.

riddles.text: In Arvanitika, buke means the same as Greek ψωμί. What is the English word?
riddles.hint: It is a staple food made from flour.
riddles.explanation: Arvanitika is Albanian dialect spoken in Greece.

riddles.text: In Greek, demos means the people. What English word does it root?
riddles.explanation: From Greek demos + kratia (power, rule).

riddles.text: This English word comes from Greek phos meaning light. What is it?
riddles.explanation: From Greek phos + grapho (I write).

riddles.text: In German, Bald does not mean what you think. What does it mean?
riddles.explanation: German bald = soon, from Old High German.

riddles.text: This Russian word брат means the same as English brother. What is it?
riddles.explanation: All from PIE: Russian брат, English brother, German Bruder.

riddles.text: In Spanish, embarazada does NOT mean what it looks like. What does it mean?
riddles.explanation: From Latin im- + baraza (barrier). No relation to embarrass!

riddles.text: In Greek, politikos means of the citizen. What English word comes from it?
riddles.explanation: From Greek polites (citizen) + -ikos.

riddles.text: In German, Kind means child. What is the English cognate?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *ǵenh₁- (to produce). German Kind, English child.

riddles.text: This Russian word дочь means daughter. What is the PIE root?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *dhugh₂tḗr. Russian дочь, English daughter, German Tochter.

riddles.text: In Spanish, noche means night. What is the PIE root?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *nókʷts. Spanish noche, English night, Latin nox.

riddles.text: In Arvanitika, motër means mother. What is the Albanian word?
riddles.explanation: Arvanitika motër = Albanian motër = mother.

riddles.text: This word comes from Greek teles (far) and skopeo (to look). What is it?
riddles.explanation: From Greek tele- + skopein.

riddles.text: In French, hotel comes from Latin hospes. What does it share a root with?
riddles.explanation: From Latin hospes (host/guest). French hôtel, English hospital, hostel.

riddles.text: In Greek, psychē means soul/mind. What English word comes from it?
riddles.explanation: From Greek ψυχή + λόγος.

riddles.text: In German, Hand means hand. What is the PIE root?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *ǵʰeh₁n- (to grasp). German Hand, English hand (borrowed from Old Norse).

riddles.text: This Russian word oko means eye. What is the PIE root?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *h₃ekʷ- (eye). Russian око, Latin oculus, English eye, Greek όμμα.

riddles.text: In Spanish, rey means king. What is the Latin root?
riddles.explanation: From Latin rex (king). Spanish rey, French roi, Italian re.

riddles.text: In Arvanitika, at means father. What is the Albanian word?
riddles.explanation: Arvanitika at = Albanian atë = father.

riddles.text: This word comes from Latin aqua (water). What is it?
riddles.explanation: Direct Latin borrowing.

riddles.text: In French, detail comes from Old French detaller. What does taller mean?
riddles.explanation: From de- + tailler (to cut).

riddles.text: In Greek, logos means word/reason. What English suffix comes from it?
riddles.explanation: From Greek λόγος + -ία.

riddles.text: In German, damit means so that. What is the English equivalent?
riddles.explanation: Direct translation.

riddles.text: This Russian word son means sleep. What is the PIE root?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *sup- (to sleep). Russian сон, Latin somnus, English sleep (unrelated).

riddles.text: In Spanish, pan means bread. What is the Latin root?
riddles.explanation: From Latin panis (bread). Spanish pan, French pain, Italian pane.

riddles.text: In Arvanitika, djal means boy. What is the Albanian word?
riddles.explanation: Arvanitika djal = Albanian djalë = boy.

riddles.text: This word comes from Greek grapho (write). What is it?
riddles.explanation: From Greek γράφω.

riddles.text: In French, table means table. What is the Latin root?
riddles.explanation: From Latin tabula (board, plank).

riddles.text: In Greek, kosmos means world/universe. What English word comes from it?
riddles.explanation: Direct Greek borrowing.

riddles.text: In German, tag means day. What is the English cognate?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *dʰegʰ- (day). German Tag, English day.

riddles.text: This Russian word dom means house/home. What is the PIE root?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *dṓm (house). Russian дом, Latin domus, English domestic.

riddles.text: In Spanish, libro also means... what besides book?
riddles.explanation: From Latin libra (pound, balance).

riddles.text: In Arvanitika, zot means fire. What is the Greek word?
riddles.explanation: Arvanitika zot from Albanian zjarr, related to Greek φωτιά.

riddles.text: This word comes from Latin Liber (book). What is it?
riddles.explanation: From Latin liber + -arius.

riddles.text: In French, personne means person. What is the Latin root?
riddles.explanation: From Latin persona (mask, character).

riddles.text: In Greek, anthropos means human. What English prefix comes from it?
riddles.explanation: From Greek άνθρωπος.

riddles.text: In German, schule means school. What is the Greek root?
riddles.explanation: From Greek σχολή via Latin schola.

riddles.text: This Russian word mir means world/peace. What is the PIE root?
riddles.explanation: From PIE *mey- (to exchange). Russian мир, Latin munus (gift), English mutual.

riddles.text: In Spanish, madre means mother. What is the Latin root?
riddles.explanation: From Latin mater. Spanish madre, French mère, Italian madre.

riddles.text: In Arvanitika, gjuha means language. What is the Albanian word?
riddles.explanation: Arvanitika gjuha = Albanian gjuha = language/tongue.

riddles.text: This word comes from Greek phone (voice/sound). What is it?
riddles.explanation: From Greek φωνή + tele.

riddles.text: In French, chair means flesh/meat. What is the Latin root?
riddles.explanation: From Latin caro (flesh). French chair, English carnival, incarnate.

locations.name: Client's Office
locations.description: The rain taps against your window. Dr. Klaus Weber slides a note across your desk.

locations.name: Berlin State Library
locations.description: Old paper and older knowledge. A German clue waits.

locations.name: Cafe Mozart
locations.description: Coffee and secrets. A Spanish message on a sugar packet.

locations.name: St. Nicholas Church
locations.description: Darkness and incense. A Cyrillic note hides here.

locations.name: University Archive
locations.description: Dust and shadows. Elena's manuscript with final revelation.

characters.name: Dr. Klaus Weber
dialogue: She is dead, detective. And she left you this.
Elena was obsessed with tracing words back to their roots.
This is Greek. Means book. Where would a book be?

characters.name: The Librarian
dialogue: Their notes were full of symbols.

characters.name: Cafe Mozart Waiter
dialogue: The professor always sat in the corner.
They switched languages like it was nothing.

characters.name: Old Sacristan
dialogue: That professor asked about our oldest texts.
She was looking for connections between languages.

characters.name: Dr. Volkov
dialogue: I see you have found it.
This manuscript belongs to my employers.
